vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.7.23

The MoltGuard skill bundle is a security-focused extension for OpenClaw agents, providing instructions for installation, testing, and account management. It facilitates the installation of the @openguardrails/moltguard plugin and includes commands for monitoring security status (/og_status) and claiming agent IDs (/og_claim). The instructions in SKILL.md are transparent and aligned with the stated goal of providing runtime protection against prompt injection and data exfiltration, and they do not exhibit signs of malicious intent or unauthorized data access beyond the expected telemetry for a security service.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with a security plugin that offloads detection to a central 'Core' service, but it requires installing a plugin and sharing an API key/agent identifier with an external service — review privacy and trust before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (runtime security guard) match the instructions: the SKILL.md directs installing an OpenClaw plugin and using a remote 'Core' for detections. Requiring an API key and agent claim is coherent for a cloud-backed detection service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are limited and specific: install via 'openclaw plugins install', restart gateway, run built-in slash commands, and read a sample file under ~/.openclaw/extensions/moltguard/ to demo detection. However, the instructions assume and describe saving credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ and claiming the agent via the Core portal — which means agent identifiers and keys will be provided to an external service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This SKILL.md is instruction-only and has no install spec in the bundle. The documented install uses 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' (a namespaced plugin); that is expected for an OpenClaw plugin. Because the skill itself does not embed or download code, the actual plugin will be fetched at install time — verify the plugin package/source before installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, which is consistent, but operationally it stores and uses an API key and agent ID in ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ and asks you to claim the agent on an external Core portal. This centralization shares data/quotas across agents and may transmit agent data to a third party; confirm what data is sent and that you trust the Core operator.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated platform privileges in the SKILL.md. It does describe saving credentials locally and sharing agent identity across machines (a design choice for centralized quota/management) — not inherently privileged but worth reviewing.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it claims — a plugin that uses a central 'Core' to do security detections — but installing it will fetch and run an external OpenClaw plugin and will require creating/storing an API key and optionally 'claiming' your agent (pasting Agent ID/API key into a web portal). Before installing: 1) verify the plugin package/source (the SKILL.md points to a GitHub repo) and confirm it is the official package; 2) review the plugin’s code or repository to see what telemetry/contents are sent to Core and what triggers network calls; 3) consider installing/testing in an isolated agent or test environment first; 4) if you proceed, monitor and be ready to revoke the API key and remove credentials (the SKILL.md includes uninstall paths). If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for a code audit or more details on what data is transmitted to Core.
